standard.title: Changing and caring for places
standard.description: how places change and how they can be cared for by different groups including First Nations Australians
standard.prior_knowledge: From Foundation (AC9HSFK03): Students identified features of places and how places can be looked after. From AC9HS1K03: Students classified local place features as natural, managed or constructed.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain how places change and how they can be cared for by different groups including First Nations Australians.

nodes.label: How places change
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and describe examples of how local places change, including changes caused by weather, seasons, erosion and human activity.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe at least two ways a local place has changed or could change (e.g. erosion, new buildings, revegetation).
nodes.typical_width: Observe and describe changes to natural, managed and constructed features in local places; distinguish changes caused by natural processes (seasons, erosion) from those caused by human activity (construction, clearing); compare current observations with past photographs.
wider: Track change in a specific local place over time using photographs, drawings and observations across seasons
Investigate how a significant environmental change (e.g. clearing, flooding) affected a local place and what happened as a result
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding how places change is prerequisite to understanding why they need care — students who cannot identify change mechanisms cannot explain the need for care actions in Node 2.

response_modes.reason: Change is most visible through direct observation and photograph comparison — multiple change examples across natural and human-caused change gives students the range needed.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two ways a local place has changed
Distinguishes at least one natural change from one human-caused change

nodes.label: Caring for places — why and how
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe how and why local places are cared for, and identify who is responsible for different types of care.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe at least two ways a local place can be cared for and explain why that care is needed.
nodes.typical_width: Describe how local features and places are cared for; connect care actions to specific change risks (e.g. not walking in muddy areas, watering plants in dry weather); identify who provides care and why.
wider: Investigate First Nations Australian practices of managing and caring for Country/Place and explain how these practices work
Compare how different groups (council, community, Traditional Owners) care for the same place and discuss similarities and differences

response_modes.reason: First Nations Australian caring practices offer a qualitatively distinct model of care — integrate this alongside local council and community examples for genuine breadth.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: First Nations Australian land care practices (fire, rotational use, seasonal management) represent a sophisticated and contextually different approach to caring for places that enriches all students' understanding of stewardship.
success_criteria: Describes at least two care actions for a local place
Explains why each care action is needed, connecting it to a change risk

nodes.label: Reduce, reuse, recycle — local systems
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify what local resources can be recycled, reduced or reused, and describe the local systems (rules, signs, collection) that support these activities.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least three resources that can be recycled, reduced or reused and name one local system that supports these activities.
nodes.typical_width: Distinguish between recyclable, reducible and reusable resources; identify local spaces and systems (waste collection routes, signs, rules) that support sustainable use; connect resource management to caring for places.
wider: Investigate how local government waste management systems work and who is responsible for each part
Compare resource management practices at home, at school and in the wider community

response_modes.reason: This node connects caring-for-places principles to concrete local civic systems — an integration of geographic stewardship with civic knowledge.

success_criteria: Identifies resources that can be recycled, reduced or reused with examples
Names at least one local system that supports sustainable resource management
